title: AgentOS: choose the workspace
question: Compare the layout schematics, not just the colors. Every direction includes open-ended chat, a live decision graph, Hermes connection, usage metrics, and pause controls. This choice approves the design direction, not unfinished backend capabilities.

options.label: Signal Desk
options.lineage: Audio signal-routing consoles, translated into a calm execution workspace
options.thesis: The conversation sets the task; the graph shows the work as it happens.
options.viewport: A quiet conversation lane occupies the left third, a large branching graph fills the right, Hermes sits in the header, and tokens, cost, time, and Pause share one fixed bottom strip.
options.risk: A graph-first workspace needs a strong empty state so a new user immediately knows where to type.

raised.raise: Every node has the same label, status, duration, and disclosure positions, making a dense run scannable.
Inactive surfaces stay flat and neutral; emphasis is reserved for the current work and user decisions.
State uses text, symbols, and connector form together, never color alone.
Selecting a branch preserves its context instead of zooming the rest of the workflow out of recognition.

options.label: Run Notebook
options.lineage: Experiment notebooks and chronological execution records
options.thesis: Each request becomes one readable record: task, execution graph, result.
options.viewport: One wide conversation column contains an expandable graph for the current request; a narrow status rail holds Hermes, usage, and Pause, and the composer stays anchored below.
options.risk: Familiar and easy to learn, but closer to conventional chatbot layouts; the graph must earn its distinctive role.

options.label: Route Map
options.lineage: Transit diagrams with disciplined branches and interchange points
options.thesis: Follow the path from your request to its outcome, and inspect the decisions at each junction.
options.viewport: A request strip and Hermes control sit above a full-width graph; the active path is emphasized, an inspector opens on selection, and the composer and usage controls sit below.
options.case: Strong at explaining branches and parallel tasks to judges; less conversational than Signal Desk during a long exchange.
options.risk: Connections must reflect real dependencies; attractive route lines cannot invent task relationships.

options.label: Execution Board
options.lineage: Departure-board information grids, without novelty flap animations
options.thesis: Read the run at a glance: which tasks are active, what they cost, and what is waiting.
options.viewport: The prompt and Hermes control head a board of aligned task rows, while a linked graph occupies the lower half and the composer, totals, and Pause remain fixed.
options.case: Strongest at comparing timings and spotting bottlenecks; weaker than Signal Desk at maintaining a simple chatbot experience.
options.risk: Could feel like a monitoring console unless secondary columns stay collapsed until requested.

options.label: Archive
options.thesis: Each run is a labeled container that opens to reveal its execution.
options.viewport: Stacked run labels open into graph and conversation detail.
options.case: Useful for history, but the archive metaphor is unfamiliar for asking a new question and hides the live task.
options.kept: Consistent node anatomy for scanning dense runs.
options.risk: Container animation adds friction to immediate execution.

options.label: Clear Field
options.thesis: An almost white canvas isolates one active observation at a time.
options.viewport: A large current-decision field is edged by quiet chat and measurement panels.
options.case: The atmospheric metaphor adds no familiar way to understand task dependencies or control execution.
options.kept: Inactive surfaces remain quiet rather than competing with the active decision.
options.risk: Spectral accents risk becoming decoration unrelated to product state.

options.label: Precision Rail
options.thesis: Every decision registers against one precise execution rail.
options.viewport: A single rail holds decision marks, opening one large task detail above it.
options.case: Its abstract controls are harder to learn, and a single rail obscures parallel work compared with an explicit graph.
options.kept: Status must remain legible through labels and form, not color alone.
options.risk: Tiny calibrated marks would weaken presentation-distance readability.

options.label: Atlas
options.thesis: Explore a run as a field of related observations.
options.viewport: A wide navigable field of task markers opens focused node details.
options.case: Constellations suggest similarity rather than dependency, and offer less familiar task controls than an explicit workflow graph.
options.kept: Focus a branch while preserving surrounding context.
options.risk: An ornamental star field would make workflow structure less trustworthy.

canonCard.label: Conventional chat workspace
canonCard.thesis: A familiar chatbot layout with a graph tab and standard inspector.
canonCard.viewport: Conversation in the center, history on the left, and optional graph and metrics on the right.
canonCard.risk: Easy to recognize, but deliberately less distinctive.
